name: Ellerbuilt Woodworks
old_description: Driven by a deep respect for the creative process and an unwavering commitment to doing what is right, Ellerbuilt was founded on a simple, powerful idea: if you are going to spend your life creating, you should pour everything you have into it. Every table, every project, every piece is the result of patience, purpose, and an artist’s relentless pursuit of excellence — even when no one is watching.
about:
Ellerbuilt Woodworks operates from Carson City, Nevada, where founder Brandon Eller established the shop as an extension of a lifelong dedication to woodworking. Eller’s path began with childhood projects — refinishing a bench at age ten — and deepened through study of Japanese joinery traditions. The business emerged from a philosophy that craftsmanship should reflect the maker’s full attention, not merely fill a space.

The shop produces custom cabinetry and handcrafted furniture for residential interiors. Offerings span kitchen and bathroom cabinets, built-in shelving and wall units, home-office desks and partner desks, bedroom pieces such as headboards and dressers, plus kitchen islands, bar cabinets, and entertainment centers. Work combines traditional hand-tool techniques with modern machinery, and finishes include conversion varnish, catalyzed lacquer, and UV-cured coatings. Wood selection ranges from domestic hardwoods — oak, maple, cherry, walnut — to softwoods like redwood and cedar and exotic species.

Clients are homeowners, designers, and builders seeking made-to-measure woodwork for kitchens, baths, offices, bedrooms, and entertainment areas. Each project starts with a site visit and design consultation, followed by a detailed timeline; smaller jobs may finish in weeks, while larger commissions can require several months.

Ellerbuilt distinguishes itself through an uncompromising standard: “If something is easy to do, it’s not worth doing.” Eller visits every installation space, designs for exact fit, and insists on joinery and finishing that will endure generations. The shop’s differentiator is not speed or volume but the deliberate, risk-accepting pursuit of pieces that carry the maker’s signature.
